about: Drives under flake quarantine (test-suite restructure, 2026-11-09; the flake rule lives in tests/TIER-MAP.md). A quarantined drive is removed from the Tier A core set and from Tier B family sets by scripts/select-tier.py: it does not gate the fast tiers until it is hardened and Andrew (or the round that hardens it) removes the entry. It still runs - and still gates - in the Tier C full battery and the nightly battery, where its surface matters most and a flake is handled by the one-focused-re-run rule. Entry requires TWO flake records under the new rule, or a standing record of repeated flakes from the audit sweep.

quarantined.reason: Repeated FLAKE-classified failures in the 2026-11-09 audit sweep (the T3 family across the census-fix round and earlier). Excluded from Tier A gating per the restructure ruling until hardened; its finish/Undo guard coverage lives in drive146 C0/C1b in the meantime, and drive89 itself still runs at Tier C and nightly.

S2a failed-settle flake, same signature twice (test-suite flake rule: two flakes = quarantine + harden). Flake #1: Beta 1.159 battery run 42738499028 attempt 1 - a wholly-failed grid settled DEGRADED instead of failed; the focused re-run (attempt 2) passed 19/19. Flake #2: Beta 1.160 battery run 42746665514 - the same grid settled READY instead of failed (S2b cascaded); the focused re-run (dispatched battery 42747758567) passed 19/19. Root cause (drive181-harden round, 2026-11-09): TEST class, not APP - the app's restore-from-cache settle was correct both times; the drive's cache wipe (jWipe) resolved on IndexedDB onblocked/onerror as if the wipe had succeeded and was never verified, while the app's fire-and-forget cache-write queue (crCacheQueue - its writes always land, by design) can leave the Vaughan record in place or re-land it behind the delete, so S2's prepare restored a full record (ready) or a partial one (degraded) instead of fetching against the failure stub. Quarantined from Tier A/B gating until the hardened wipe (queue drain + true-completion delete + verified-empty read) proves out; still runs at Tier C and nightly.
